restated: (∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, |Real.log (triangleRamseyNumber k : ℝ)| ≤ c * |(k : ℝ) * Real.log (k : ℝ)|) ∧ (∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, |(k : ℝ) * Real.log (k : ℝ)| ≤ c * |Real.log (triangleRamseyNumber k : ℝ)|)
english: There are constants c, c' such that for all sufficiently large k: |log R_k(3)| ≤ c·|k log k| and |k log k| ≤ c'·|log R_k(3)|. That is, log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k), i.e. R_k(3) = k^Θ(k).
why_clearer: Replaces Mathlib's =Θ[atTop] notation with explicit constants and 'for all large k'.

restated: ∃ (bound : Polynomial ℕ) (verifier : List Bool × List Bool → Bool), Nonempty (VerifierTM verifier) ∧ ∀ input : List Bool, (language input = true ↔ ∃ certificate : List Bool, certificate.length ≤ bound.eval input.length ∧ verifier (input, certificate) = true)
english: A language is in NP exactly when there is a polynomial bound p and a polynomial-time Turing-machine verifier V such that x is in the language iff some certificate of length at most p(|x|) makes V accept (x, certificate).
why_clearer: OpenAI encodes 'is in NP' as a Bool built with classical `decide`; this unwraps it into the textbook certificate definition of NP.

restated: (∀ g ∈ F, ∀ h ∈ F, normalizedHamming (M.action (g * h)) (M.action g * M.action h) < ε) ∧ (∀ g ∈ F, g ≠ 1 → 1 - ε < normalizedHamming (M.action g) 1)
proof:
constructor
· rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
  exact ⟨h1, h2⟩
· rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
  exact ⟨h1, h2⟩
english: A permutation model M is ε-good on a finite set F exactly when (1) it is ε-almost multiplicative on F: M(gh) and M(g)M(h) disagree on fewer than an ε-fraction of points, and (2) it is (1−ε)-separating: every non-identity g ∈ F moves more than a (1−ε)-fraction of points.
why_clearer: Shows the two hidden conditions packed inside the structure as one explicit statement.

english: The normalized Hamming distance of two permutations is the fraction of points of Y on which they disagree.
why_clearer: Unfolds Mathlib's hammingDist on functions into the familiar 'fraction of disagreements'.
